{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Simpler buying path. A's payer is the same solo founder who feels the pain, at a sourced $29–49/mo anchor (Tax Threshold Radar, Quaderno). B's payer is an eng lead buying per seat for a team, and B's own brief says the purchase likely hinges on a SOC2/SSO/retention posture a solo builder cannot provide in 90 days.",
    "Cheaper, better-targeted channel. A cites ~$0.52 CPC from $2,000 of newsletter sponsorship in the exact target community. B's channels are a Product Hunt launch costing $3,300–$6,000 in founder time and Google Ads at ~$650 per devtools SQL, which is expensive for one person chasing a first customer.",
    "Better-supported build feasibility. A points to a near-identical, solo-scale, monitoring-only product as evidence the scope is buildable. B's six-week buildability claim is explicitly marked [unsourced], so it counts as missing.",
    "Both face $0 anchors, but B's is worse. A competes with free monitors used as funnels for paid filing. B competes with Slack Code bundled free into every Slack plan, plus at least five direct competitors including an open-source one, all launched in the same window. That makes a standalone paid wedge harder to find.",
    "Lower compliance burden. A's liability risk can be partly scoped through read-only APIs and no filing. B needs a security and data-retention posture before enterprise pilots, which adds cost and delay before any first payment."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's core feasibility claim, that a thin session-relay plus presence/handoff layer is buildable solo in six weeks, is marked [unsourced]. The YC Fall 2026 RFS demand signal also has no citation. Meanwhile, B's two demand quotes describe agent invisibility and observability, not a willingness to pay for multiplayer steering or handoff.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. A has serious unresolved risks: free monitoring from Kintsugi, Numeral and TaxJar; founders moving to Merchants of Record instead; and an unverified comparable, since Tax Threshold Radar's testimonials could not be confirmed and it may be only a landing page. A's demand quotes are also thin: one is from 2020 and the other is undated, so the claimed 2020–2025 span is not fully supported. A wins mainly because B's go-to-market, security bar and competitive density look worse for a one-person, 90-day first-customer goal, not because A's demand is proven."
}
